props.gloss_en: bundles of straw, wood and twigs: one may not roof a sukkah with them
one who hollows out a grain-stack to make himself a sukkah: it is not a sukkah
R' Yochanan: of the two halakhot (bundles; the hollowed stack) one is due to the storehouse decree and one to 'you shall make' and not from what is already made -- the two rest on DIFFERENT reasons

R' Yochanan: why may one not roof with bundles? at times a man comes from the field with his bundle on his shoulder and lays it on his sukkah to dry it, and then decides to use it as roofing -- and the Torah said 'you shall make', not from what is already made
R' Yirmeya: the bundles ruling is due to the storehouse decree
R' Yirmeya: so the hollowed-stack ruling is due to 'you shall make, not from what is already made'
where the mishnah says 'one may not roof with them', it is ab initio, for the storehouse decree; by Torah law it is fine
where it says 'it is not a sukkah', even after the fact, by Torah law too it is not a sukkah
one who roofed with convex (male) arrow shafts: valid
with concave (female) arrow shafts: invalid
taught by the ruling: we do not decree against convex shafts on account of concave ones
taught by the ruling: a receptacle made to be (permanently) filled IS a receptacle
roofed with combed flax: invalid
with flax stalks: valid
one may roof with licorice leaves
Rav Yehuda: wormwood leaves too may be used for roofing
Abaye: one may not roof with wormwood leaves
the reason: since their smell turns foul, one abandons the sukkah and leaves
one may roof with thorns
Rav Chanan bar Rava: shrubs too may be used for roofing
Abaye: one may not roof with shrubs
the reason: since their leaves drop, one abandons the sukkah and leaves
one may roof with the palm's offshoot (branches growing from one stem)
though they are bound, a binding by the hand of Heaven is not called a binding
though one then binds them, binding what is (already) one is not called a binding
one may roof with reed offshoots
the baraita as worded: reeds and spades (dukranin) may be used for roofing
the baraita as emended: reeds of offshoots may be used for roofing
with the bitter herbs of the marsh a person fulfils his Passover obligation
hyssop -- and not Greek, stibium, desert or Roman hyssop, nor any hyssop with a modifying name
Abaye: whatever had its name differentiated before the giving of the Torah, and the Torah was particular about it -- that is known to have a modifying name
Abaye: and these (bitter herbs) were not differentiated by name before the giving of the Torah at all
Rava: their name is plain 'bitter herbs'; they are called 'of the marsh' only because they are found in the marsh
Rav Chisda: binding three is called a binding
Rav Chisda: binding two is the dispute of R' Yosei and the Rabbis
the hyssop mishnah: the mitzva of hyssop is three stalks bearing three stems
R' Yosei: the mitzva of hyssop is three stems, its remnants two, and its stumps any amount
three stalks are required only for the mitzva ab initio; two suffice after the fact
three stalks are indispensable; with fewer the hyssop is invalid
(entertained) from R' Yosei's 'remnants two', his beginning may also be two and his 'three' is for the mitzva -- so for the Rabbis three is indispensable
R' Yosei (baraita): hyssop beginning with two and remaining one is invalid; it is valid only beginning with three and remaining two
reverse: for R' Yosei three is indispensable; for the Rabbis three is for the mitzva
the baraita: hyssop beginning with two and remaining one is valid
the baraita as worded: it is invalid only when its beginning and its remnants are one
emended: invalid only when its beginning, like its remnants, is one
Mareimar: one may roof with these Sura bundles
though they are bound, they are bound merely for counting
R' Abba: willow huts, once their top ties are undone, are valid
Rav Pappa: R' Abba speaks where he unties them (below too)
Rav Huna b. R' Yehoshua: any binding not made for carrying is not called a binding
the greens with which one fulfils the Passover obligation convey (corpse) impurity
and they do not interpose against impurity
and they disqualify a sukkah as airspace
the reason: since when they dry they crumble and fall, they are as if absent
one who harvests grapes for the winepress: they have no handles
one who harvests (grain) for roofing: it has no handles
but one who harvests for roofing -- it has handles, since he wants them (the ears) to weigh down the roofing so it does not scatter
all the more so one harvesting grapes: he does not want the stems, lest they absorb his wine
fig branches with figs, vines with grapes, straw with ears, palm branches with dates -- if the waste exceeds the food, valid; otherwise invalid
Acherim: (invalid) unless the straw exceeds the handles and the food together
(entertained) Rav Menashya bar Gadda's version is a tannaitic dispute: Acherim hold produce cut for roofing has handles, the first tanna that it has none
for R' Abba's version (the kotzer has handles) it certainly is a tannaitic dispute
the baraita deals with one who cut them for food and then decided to use them for roofing
(proposed) the Rabbis hold that once he decided to roof with them, his first intent (food) is void
all vessels enter impurity by thought and leave it only by a change through an act; an act negates act and thought, thought negates neither
(proposed) that holds of vessels, which are significant; handles, which exist only for eating, become handles by thought and cease by thought
all handles of food that one בססן on the threshing floor are pure
and R' Yosei renders them (susceptible to) impure
here too (the baraita): where he actually trampled them
Acherim's reason (on the trampling okimta): they state their view according to R' Yosei
Reish Lakish: (R' Yosei renders them impure) since they are fit for turning (the grain) with a pitchfork
here they are fit for when he dismantles (the roofing), to hold them by their stalks
R' Yochanan: בססן means actually trampled
R' Elazar: בססן means he untied their binding
R' Elazar: the prayer of the righteous is likened to a pitchfork
as the pitchfork turns the grain on the threshing floor from place to place, so the prayer of the righteous turns the mind of the Holy One from the attribute of cruelty to the attribute of mercy

questions.gloss_en: R' Yochanan (via Rabba bar bar Chana): roofing with hushnei of flax -- I do not know its status. Left open; the text records no תיקו.
Rabba bar bar Chana: and what hushnei itself denotes I do not know -- crushed but not combed, or perhaps even soaked but not crushed. Left open; no תיקו.

objections.gloss_en: אטו חבילי קש ... משום תעשה ולא מן העשוי ליכא? והחוטט בגדיש משום גזרת אוצר ליכא? -- both reasons seem to apply to both cases

objections.gloss_en: מיתיבי: hyssop -- not any hyssop with a modifying name; so 'bitter herbs of the marsh', a modified name, should not qualify

answered_by.gloss_en: a modifying name is one differentiated before Sinai; bitter herbs were never so differentiated (= p_abaye_shem_levai, p_merarita_lo_nishtana)
their name is plain bitter herbs; 'of the marsh' only says where they grow (= p_rava_merarita_stam)

objections.gloss_en: והתניא רבי יוסי אומר: two-and-one invalid, valid only three-and-two -- so R' Yosei's three is indispensable; the mapping is reversed (איפוך)
שייריו אחד פסול? הא אמרת שייריו אחד כשר! -- the seifa implies remnants of one are invalid, against the reisha

answered_by.gloss_en: אלא אימא: עד שתהא תחלתו כשייריו אחד (= p_baraita_ezov_seifa_emended)

objections.gloss_en: והא אגידי מתתאי! -- but they are still bound below

answered_by.gloss_en: דשרי להו -- he unties them (= p_dsharei_lehu)
אפילו תימא דלא שרי להו: a binding not made for carrying is no binding (= p_eged_lo_letaltel)

objections.gloss_en: אי קצצן לאכילה, מאי טעמייהו דרבנן? -- cut for food they have handles; what makes the first tanna lenient?

answered_by.gloss_en: הכא נמי שבססן ממש -- he actually trampled them, an act (= p_okimta_bsasan_mamash)

objections.gloss_en: ומי בטלה ליה מחשבה בהכי? והתנן: ... מחשבה אינה מוציאה לא מיד מעשה ולא מיד מחשבה

answered_by.gloss_en: וכי תימא: that is for vessels, which are significant; handles, which serve eating, go by thought (= p_yadot_bemachshava_salka, itself attacked from the handles mishnah -- see header)

objections.gloss_en: והתנן: כל ידות האוכלין שבססן בגורן טהורות -- בשלמא למאן דאמר בססן התיר אגודן שפיר, אלא למאן דאמר בססן ממש מאי איכא למימר? (14a.3): on that reading handles leave their status only by an act
האי מאי? there R' Yosei's reason is that the handles are fit for turning with a pitchfork; here what are they fit for?

answered_by.gloss_en: חזיא לכי סתר, למנקט להו בגילייהו (= p_chazya_lechi_satar)

objections.gloss_en: בשלמא לרבי (אליעזר) ... היינו דמטמא רבי יוסי; אלא לרבי יוחנן דאמר בססן ממש, אמאי מטמא רבי יוסי?
